component.name: TextVN
component.summary: Vietnamese Input Method Engine for Linux (Fcitx5 & IBus)

description.p: TextVN (LBS Viet Nam) is a high-performance, modern Vietnamese input method engine for Linux, designed for flawless compatibility with Wayland and X11 across GNOME, KDE Plasma, and other desktop environments.
Features:

ul.li: Support for Telex, VNI, VIQR, and customizable input methods.
First-class Wayland support via Fcitx5 (text-input-v3) without key grab issues.
Native IBus engine integration for Ubuntu GNOME desktops.
Smart application compatibility engine preventing duplicate character bugs in address bars, terminals, and games.
Classic Vietnamese input method control panel layout.

description.p: Office-productivity pack (on-device): case-adaptive text macros (hd/Hd/HD expand to lowercase/capitalised/UPPERCASE, deliberate casing preserved), spreadsheet formula guard (=sum/=if/=vlookup typed at the start of a cell are no longer accent-mangled while the VNI input method keeps working), money shorthand (=15450000d+Tab → 15.450.000 đồng, …vnd → VNĐ, …bc → accounting-grade Vietnamese words), office collocation fixes (bổ xung→bổ sung, xử dụng→sử dụng, sát nhập→sáp nhập and more, closed list with guards for correct phrases), percent spacing (100 %→100%), coder/business identifier protection (useState/onPress/getElementById never accent-folded; KPI, EBITDA, margin, revenue restored; Tab completion keeps canonical casing), and a selection transcoder: select text and press Ctrl+Shift+F9 (Windows) to detect TCVN3 (.VnTime) / VNI-Windows / decomposed Unicode and convert it to precomposed Unicode. Detection is fail-safe — real Unicode or ambiguous input is never modified.

Three-pass deep audit of the grammar assistant, closing the last false-positive classes: the cross-sentence word-repeat rule is disabled (it flagged correct Vietnamese like "…cho anh. Anh xem…"); diacritic-less Vietnamese ("an toan la quan trong") is recognised through a 1,061-entry Vietnamese ASCII syllable list so the a/an rule never rewrites it; a/an exception lists match word stems (an hourglass/honorable/heirloom), add missing /juː/ words (a Unicode string, a euphemism) and grouped number readings (an 1100/an 1850 = eleven/eighteen hundred); 31 office file extensions are masked (report.pdf never gets a space inserted); curly quotes “ ” and Vietnamese capital abbreviations (ĐH.) are handled; a double space before an inline # comment or aligned code lines is never flagged. Cross-platform: Fcitx5 fresh installs have the assistant ON like every other platform, the global-AND-override switch semantics match Windows on macOS and Linux, the fewer-than-3-words gate applies everywhere, and the Linux reconnect cap is 10 s. The desktop panel now scales with monitor DPI. Verified against 981 Vietnamese and 295 English clean sentences (zero false positives), a 43-case adversarial battery, and 701 automated tests.

Enter on the selected-text popup now applies "Sửa tất cả" (fix all) instead of doing nothing: previously the key was swallowed because the old apply path requires an empty selection, so pressing Enter on a keyboard-selected sentence's popup never fixed anything. Enter now behaves exactly like the fix-all button — the selected range is replaced with the corrected sentence through the same guarded session (the selection content is re-verified inside the edit lock before writing; Ctrl+Z belongs to your app) — and the corrected sentence is re-checked afterwards, so the panel hides when clean and keeps showing remaining suggestions otherwise. The next Enter inserts a newline as usual.

Grammar check on selected text: keyboard-select a sentence you are editing (Shift+arrows/Home/End) and after half a second the assistant popup appears anchored at the selection with the error total and the "Sửa tất cả" (fix all) button; clicking it replaces exactly the selected range with the corrected sentence (the selection content is re-verified inside the edit lock before writing; Ctrl+Z belongs to your app). Selecting to read or copy never triggers it — mouse selection does not pass through the key sink and Ctrl/Alt combinations are filtered out. Selections longer than 256 characters are skipped rather than half-checked. Verified by a two-pass independent audit across Notepad, Word and Chrome scenarios, and across the upgrade path where a running old-version input DLL picks up the new tray snapshot without a reboot.

Fixes the grammar assistant being completely dead for many users ("popup doesn't work, underline and correct don't work"): the input-method DLL disabled the whole assistant until the tray's first snapshot arrived; a settings file carried over from 0.2.37 or earlier kept the kill-switch off forever even after upgrading through 0.2.38-0.2.40 (a one-time migration now turns it back on exactly once — turning it off afterwards sticks); and the detection toast removed in 0.2.38 is back as an 8-second-cooldown fallback popup (bottom-right) for apps where the caret panel cannot anchor. Verified end-to-end by an independent audit agent across an 11-gate table; benchmarks unchanged (0/981 Vietnamese and 0/295 English false positives).

Full three-platform audit round by parallel expert agents (24 findings). Critical fixes: the article rule could corrupt real Vietnamese words ("an khang" was auto-corrected to "a khang") — in Vietnamese sentences it now requires another English indicator word; UNESCO-class acronyms (read /juː/) no longer accept the wrong article; the macOS input-method default now matches the settings UI (highlight) so upgraded users actually get the assistant; Linux fresh installs default to highlight too; the IPC wire name for article_an is registered on Linux. Panel behavior: after any fix the panel re-checks the corrected sentence and either updates with the remaining issues or disappears when clean; a new assist.display.hide_on_auto_fix option hides the popup entirely while auto-correct mode is running; clicking a non-interactive area inside the panel now dismisses it, and the first click on the pre-selected issue selects rather than applies (no accidental edits). Tray toasts are auto-fix-only with a 60-second cooldown on all platforms. Performance measured on the real engine: 14-52 µs per check, two hundred times under budget. Benchmarks unchanged: 0/981 Vietnamese and 0/295 English false positives, 100% recall.

The grammar-assistant popup is now fully mouse-driven: a "Sửa tất cả" (fix all) button applies the whole-sentence correction with the 5-second Ctrl+Z undo, clicking an underlined word or an issue row selects that suggestion, and clicking it again applies the fix. Clicks inside the popup no longer dismiss it (only outside clicks do). Auto-correct mode keeps fixing qualifying sentences automatically at the sentence end as before. Vietnamese and English corpora unchanged: 0/981 and 0/295 false positives, 100% recall.

The grammar assistant is now enabled by default in suggest-only mode (auto-fix stays opt-in and the tray/menu switch still turns it off instantly). It now covers English and office-style mixed Vietnamese/English sentences end to end: the popup at the caret shows the typed sentence with red underlines under each wrong word plus a Grammarly-style total ("N lỗi trong câu vừa gõ"), replacing the frequent tray toast — that toast now appears only when auto-fix rewrote a sentence (at most once per 60 seconds, always with the Ctrl+Z hint). Vietnamese false-positive rate stays 0/981 and English 0/295 on the labeled real-text corpora with 100% recall on both labeled error sets.

English grammar assistant (v1): sentences dominated by English are now checked — a new article rule fixes "a apple" to "an apple" by sound with closed exception lists (a university, an hour, an MBA, a NATO, an 8-bit), and the duplicate-word rule learns English-valid repeats (that that, had had, very very) while still catching real errors. Office-style mixed Vietnamese/English sentences ("vui lòng check lại file report nhé", "Anh gửi report cho team ASAP") are now covered — previously silently skipped. Four live Vietnamese-side bugs fixed: auto-inserting spaces inside abbreviations and domains (e.g., a.m., U.S., example.com), spaced ellipsis, and capitalizing code or list markers. Word completion gained an optional Space trigger (suggest.trigger = tab_and_space, off by default, never rewrites an already-correct word) and now draws on the full 3000-word frequency dictionary. Measured on labeled real-text corpora: Vietnamese 0/981 and English 0/295 false positives, recall 100% on both labeled error sets.

Grammar assistant quality audit (three full line-by-line passes). The assistant now never flags correct text: five typo-table entries whose "wrong" word is actually a valid Vietnamese word (quyến, thuở, đả, áy, điếm) were removed — they made auto-correct rewrite correct words (quyến rũ to quyển, thuở xưa to thướ). Measured on the labeled real-text corpora: false positives drop from 0.5% to 0.0% on 981 clean sentences (Wilson 0.0–0.4%), sentence recall is 83.7%, the deliberate trade of two ambiguous cases for zero false flags. Four more valid reduplications (năm năm, đâu đâu, chộp chộp, bum bum) are whitelisted, and all-caps accented Vietnamese sentences are now recognized for checking.

Linux packaging for distribution stores: an Arch/AUR package is now provided (built from source with a QA workflow that runs makepkg for real inside an Arch container, checks metadata and package contents), alongside a written analysis of why Flatpak/Snap/AppImage cannot host a system-level input method. The Fcitx5 addon now requires C++20 because Fcitx5 6.x headers use std::ranges and std::span — without it the source does not compile on rolling-release distros. macOS installation via the official Homebrew tap (brew install --cask hunglinhpt/tap/textvn) is now the recommended route, with the cask kept in sync automatically from signed release checksums.

Old-style tone placement is now the default on a fresh install on every platform (hòa, thủy, khỏe instead of hoà, thuỷ, khoẻ), together with Vietnamese typing enabled out of the box; existing settings files keep their chosen style. English typing auto-correction now covers the 3000 most frequent English words: words like text, look, download or message are typed as-is, while Vietnamese syllables that have no other Telex spelling (hải, Lê, sĩ, ơn, lá…) still win. A new cross-product regression matrix types the full common-words corpus through all sixteen combinations of output charset (precomposed Unicode, decomposed Unicode, TCVN3, VNI Windows) and input method (Telex, VNI, VIQR, Simple Telex) with hard-coded anchors from the legacy encoding tables. Backspace behavior under the new default is pinned: retyping the deleted letter rejoins the word with its tone, and pressing the same tone key again undoes it (ass → as), matching UniKey. The documentation now describes precisely when a composition underline can appear (only inside Chromium/Electron/Qt apps on Linux, drawn by the app itself). An opt-in Tab completion finishes a half-typed Vietnamese syllable into the most frequent matching syllable from a 3000-syllable frequency list (off by default via suggest.enabled).

Whole-system review after 0.2.31. The About dialog is now identical on all three platforms (a smart, multi-platform Vietnamese input method, with the version number). macOS settings now follow the shared specification: the same charset and input method labels and order as Windows and Linux, and the fixed Ctrl+Shift switch key (the macOS-only Alt+Z and Caps Lock options were removed). Linux - switching between Vietnamese and English with Ctrl+Shift or the menu no longer flips back when moving to another window (a regression since 0.2.30, IBus and Fcitx5), and Fcitx5 profiles with several groups get TextVN in the active group. Windows - the tray no longer quits when a sign-out or restart is cancelled, upgrades only stop the tray of the folder being upgraded and stop it reliably, apps still running an older input method keep receiving the Vietnamese/English switch after an upgrade, TextVN.exe --status reports OFFLINE instead of crashing, the machine uninstaller removes TextVN from the keyboard list of every signed-in account, and a rare composition error can no longer duplicate text. Release commits and tags are now signed.

Round 16 follow-up completing the three-platform audit roadmap. Windows - COM callbacks (Activate, Deactivate, ActivateEx, OnSetFocus) are wrapped in catch_unwind so a panic can no longer abort the host app, and a failed internal borrow now returns an error instead of silently succeeding (which would leak the TSF advise cookies until thread exit). macOS - AX field gathering is de-duplicated per process and uses a short messaging timeout so a hung app cannot stall detection, the field cache is bounded and prunes expired entries, the IPC server caps per-app state so a same-user flood cannot inflate RAM or overflow the snapshot frame, client identity is taken from the sender instead of the frontmost app, delegate callbacks are pinned to the main queue, the diagnostics log rotates at 1 MiB, and the dead writer-only modifier state was removed. Linux - the leftover unframed IPC receiver was removed, the GTK settings window disconnects child-window signals before freeing its state (no use-after-free on teardown), Fcitx5 activation adds the input method to the group named by the profile instead of hardcoding the first group, XDG paths must be absolute, the logger refuses silently truncated paths and uses a thread-safe time call, the Fcitx5 addon unregisters its actions on unload, and the release staging script refuses dangerous target directories before deleting anything.

Round 16 of the three-platform audit (Windows/macOS/Linux): Windows - ILOT uninstall spec normalized with the 0x prefix (keyboard auto-added by Windows is now actually removed), WOW64 mirror CTF scoped to machine installs only and stale per-user mirrors cleaned, installer stops a running tray before upgrading and the tray answers RestartManager query-end-session gracefully, mutex wait uses OpenMutex without acquiring ownership, UAC helper initializes COM, poisoned RwLocks no longer panic. macOS - composition retraction order fixed (marked text is withdrawn before real deletions, preventing lost characters on NSTextView clients), IPC client always retries after protocol violations and reconnects on focus, Alt+Z and Caps Lock switch keys now actually work in the input method, engine failures send crash reports, "Reset to defaults" preserves macros, English words, emoji and autostart, double-clicking the app always opens the running instance. Linux - IPC message dispatch locked by the type field (state keys named like message types can no longer hijack parsing), per-app overrides fall back to the base state when the app is no longer present, composition buffer overflow guard, UTF-8 decoder rejects overlong/surrogate sequences.

Clean uninstall: every uninstall path (Windows installer, portable script, Microsoft Store cleanup) now closes TextVN first and waits until it has fully exited before removing files, so a running TextVN no longer leaves files behind. Uninstalling also removes a language that TextVN itself added to the Windows language list when no other keyboard was added for it, and still gives Ctrl+Shift back to Windows. The Microsoft Store package attached to the release now carries the real Store identity.

Typing: Backspace now deletes the last visible character like UniKey instead of undoing the last key; automatic capitalization only starts a sentence after ". ! ?" followed by a space or Enter, so URLs, file names and decimals are left alone; VNI and VIQR place marks typed after a whole vowel cluster on the right vowel; Telex "w" on its own becomes "u" with horn, marks switch between circumflex and horn/breve, pressing a mark key a third time removes the mark and types the letter, and a "d" typed later in a word strokes the initial "d". English words such as sort, keep, using, music, deed and defend are no longer turned into Vietnamese-looking syllables, and Vietnamese syllables such as "thi" with tone are no longer restored to English. Linux: Fcitx5 always keeps its own addon directory, IBus starts when the install path contains spaces, "sudo ./install.sh --system" no longer touches user settings, and the GTK settings window keeps its English dictionary window. Every release asset stays signed with GPG and Sigstore, and the release pipeline now stops when signing keys are missing.

macOS: the input method reads the "Non-preedit" setting (BUG-05) when the settings app broadcasts a configuration reload - when enabled the Preedit composition strategy downgrades to BackspaceType for underline-free typing; configs missing the key keep underlined preedit. Known limitation of this release: the setting is not read when an input session starts, and the input method's strategy resolution fails so typing always uses BackspaceType; both are fixed after 0.2.27. Verified the IMK client already applies global "*" StateUpdate/Snapshot broadcasts and the app menu bar syncs via didSet. Linux docs aligned with the SEC-04 socket path priority. All release assets (Windows, Linux and macOS) are now signed with GPG detached signatures (.asc) and Sigstore keyless signatures, and SHA256SUMS.txt is clearsigned; Windows Authenticode and macOS Developer ID signing and notarization are not in place yet.

Thorough uninstall (round 13): the registry dump before/after a real uninstall revealed 27 keys still referencing the TextVN TIP after removal - the CTF Assemblies "Default" value for both languages (written when TextVN became the default input method), the InputMethodOverride value, and the entire HKLM machine tree left by an earlier machine-scope registration. Unregister now removes all of them (Assemblies defaults are enumerated and deleted when they reference the TextVN CLSID; the per-user uninstall also attempts the machine cleanup best-effort), the installer no longer skips machine unregister for per-user removals, the tray treats a machine registration pointing to a missing DLL as absent so repair re-runs, and the installer test suite now scans for any leftover TIP GUID after uninstall as a hard gate. Verified live: 27 leftover paths reduced to zero after an elevated unregister.

MSIX readiness (round 12 audit): the Store package now works as a true distribution channel. When the app runs from the WindowsApps package folder it stages its full payload (tray, CLI, TSF DLL, resources, data) to a stable per-user location and relaunches non-packaged, so TSF registration survives every Store update (the package folder name changes on each update and the old one is deleted, which used to leave the COM/CTF registration dangling) and is immune to packaged-app registry virtualization. The MSIX payload now also includes resources and data. Locked files during re-staging are handled with the rename-then-copy technique.

Line-level installer review round: the Add/Remove Programs entry now includes DisplayIcon (UninstallDisplayIcon) so the entry is fully standard, the setup executable's FileVersion string is filled in (VersionInfoTextVersion) instead of blank, and SetupLogging writes an install log to %TEMP% as the only retrievable evidence if the Store validator fails again. Per the repository owner's decision the machine-install (all-users, HKLM) build is the official Store submission; the portable zip is unchanged.

Microsoft Store identity fix (round 7): the account owner located the real Publisher display name in account settings and set it to "LinhBH.CoM" - the exact string the installer wrote all along in 0.2.16-0.2.20, meaning those earlier failures were caused by install mode (admin/740, exit 10) and the resubmission cache trap, never by the string; 0.2.21-0.2.22 had guessed a different publisher and were wrong. Lesson B18 extended: the publisher display name lives in a less obvious account page and must be verified by code point dump at the source before any identifier is trusted.

Microsoft Store root-cause fix: the Add/Remove Programs publisher is now "Linh Bui" (pure ASCII), matching the Partner Center publisher display name character-for-character. The previous attempts never matched (brand name "LinhBH.CoM", then "Linh Bi" with a Greek beta U+03B2 that was a font misread of Latin B), which is what the validator compares - lesson B18: verify identifiers by code point dump from the source of truth, never by font appearance. The machine-install variant is now a standard release asset, built and HKLM-validated by the release workflow.

Microsoft Store fix: the Add/Remove Programs publisher now matches the Partner Center publisher display name character-for-character ("Linh βùi" - the beta is U+03B2, as recorded on the Dev Center account), which is what the Store validator compares; the .iss keeps a UTF-8 BOM so the non-ASCII publisher survives compilation, and the validation harness now builds the expected publisher from code points (ASCII-only scripts) and prints code points on mismatch. Adopted /DMachineInstall=1 to build a machine-install variant validated by CI (-MachineOnly) as evidence for the HKLM hypothesis, and build-msix.ps1 warns loudly when the MSIX identity is still a placeholder.

Hardening + Store-validation round 3: the validator harness now checks the installer manifest is asInvoker and that the Add/Remove entry matches the product name, publisher and version exactly (single entry, no bundleware); the uninstaller restores the Windows Ctrl+Shift hotkey; the tray only offers the one-time UAC machine registration from trusted install folders (Program Files, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs - portable copies get a clear notice instead); the IPC named pipe is created with a current-user-only DACL; the Linux IPC client prefers $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and refuses sockets not owned by the current user; the English-restore dictionary scan filters by length before allocating.

Silent installs are now pure file copies: no language dialog on any system locale, no TSF calls in the installer process (the app self-registers on first run with a one-time UAC prompt if needed), and run-once helpers are skipped in silent mode - removing every remaining silent-install blocker for Microsoft Store validation.

Store validation round 2: machine-wide install restored (Microsoft's validator only reads the HKLM Add/Remove entry while silent installs still always exit 0), ARP display name set to exactly "TextVN", and the validation harness now enforces the HKLM entry.

Installer defaults to a per-user install (no UAC) so it passes Microsoft Store package validation in a non-elevated sandbox; silent installs always exit 0 with the app self-registering the input method on first run.

Portable builds now self-heal on Windows 11 24H2+ where per-user activation is refused: the tray offers a one-time machine-wide registration (UAC) and switches back to Vietnamese mode, so unpack-and-run works without the installer.
Unregister now also removes the input method from the modern Win+Space language list (no more ghost entries after removal) and broadcasts the standard WM_SETTINGCHANGE notification.

UI unified across all three platforms (same labels, order and buttons; enforced by a cross-platform label test), fixed per-monitor DPI sizing that clipped long labels and controls on high-scaling monitors, and consistent V/E icon colours.

English-dictionary editor on macOS and Linux (parity with Windows), macOS no longer drops the word list when saving, Linux corpus now runs in CI, and honest documentation of per-user TSF limits on Windows 11 24H2+.

Installer upgrades no longer fail with "DeleteFile failed" when the TSF DLL is loaded (rename-then-replace), the registration flow keeps TextVN in the modern Win+Space list, and activation diagnostics explain when a machine-wide install is required.
Hotfix: activating an already-active TextVN profile no longer fails (check-then-activate).

Ctrl+Shift now also switches the active input method to TextVN (mode change means typing changes), tray and engine state can no longer diverge after rapid toggles, and upgrading clears stale old-version data while preserving the user dictionary and abbreviations.

Personal English-dictionary editor in the control panel (user-added words override the ambiguity protection), documented language-priority rules, and a hardened one-command release preflight that mirrors every CI gate.

Automatic English-word detection at word boundaries (built-in common-English dictionary that never overrides common Vietnamese syllables), Tab completion for English words, Escape restores the raw keystrokes, and the settings dialog now rescales correctly when moved between monitors with different DPI.
Ctrl+Shift now toggles Vietnamese mode and the tray icon in every application (observe-only low-level detector with cross-source debounce), matching UniKey behavior.
Self-heals ghost registrations from deleted portable folders, and keeps the proven dual-language (VI + EN) layout registration after two risky layout-list experiments were reverted.
Portable build: composition display attributes now survive layout updates (no more underlines without admin), and Ctrl+Shift toggling works reliably. Adds an opt-in SignPath code-signing pipeline.
Hardens Windows TSF machine registration and per-user activation, fixes VNI digits and macro expansion, and repairs the macOS EventTap lifecycle. Unsigned release candidate.

App icons everywhere: macOS bundles and the input source menu get their icon (.icns), Linux portable mode stages hicolor icons, and the Windows Settings dialog and installer wizard use the TextVN icon. Hardened release publishing (draft-first) and CI caching.
Fixes the macOS login launch showing the Settings window at sign-in, and refreshes the macOS menu bar, per-app toggles, and Windows IME registration. Unsigned cross-platform release.
Unsigned release candidate for Windows, macOS and Linux; macOS GUI validation remains pending.
Unsigned cross-platform release candidate with synchronised package versions.
Initial release of TextVN with a compact control panel and dual Fcitx5/IBus support.
